guarantees.claim: reg_busy is assigned the value of shadow_busy, so it is always 1'b0.
unused_wdata is assigned the XOR reduction of reg_wdata to avoid lint warnings.
unused_be is assigned the XOR reduction of reg_be to avoid lint warnings.

assumptions.claim: External signal reg_we must be a single-cycle pulse when the module is not in reset.
assumptions.risk: If violated, multiple register writes may be triggered or glitches may occur.

assumptions.claim: External signal reg_re must be a single-cycle pulse when the module is not in reset.
assumptions.risk: If violated, multiple reads may be issued or internal state may be corrupted.

assumptions.claim: After a rising edge on reg_re or reg_we, tl_o_pre.d_valid must assert in the next cycle.
assumptions.risk: Violation indicates a TL-UL handshake violation, potentially stalling the response channel indefinitely.

assumptions.claim: When reg_we or reg_re is high, at most one bit of addr_hit is high ($onehot0).
assumptions.risk: Multiple registers could be accessed concurrently, causing conflicting updates or reads.

uncertain_points.claim: Parity checking on the TL-UL bus is disabled because the reqParity assume statement is commented out.
uncertain_points.cond: During any bus transaction when parity errors could occur
uncertain_points.risk: If bus parity errors occur, they may go undetected, potentially allowing silent data corruption in HMAC registers.

uncertain_points.claim: shadow_busy is tied to 0, indicating that shadow register busy status is never asserted.
uncertain_points.risk: If shadow registers are used for secure key updates, a missing busy indication could allow partial or race-condition updates.

uncertain_points.claim: reg_busy is tied to 0 (via shadow_busy), providing no busy indication for register operations.
uncertain_points.risk: Other logic expecting a busy signal may misbehave, though this may be intended for a simple register interface.
